description: Wire the atomic transition into the driving adapter (deployment/deployment.py) so every state change goes through transition_state() and no issue can end with 2+ state labels, then add integration coverage for the todo->dev->review path. This fixes the live bug from issue #107 where an issue held crewflow:todo AND crewflow:review simultaneously. Depends on FEAT-002.
steps: Study how deployment/deployment.py applies labels today: provider.set_labels(project, key, labels) REPLACES the full label set. The branches that currently edit labels are: rebrand (~line 1123: builds current_labels from result.item.labels, removes decision.remove_labels, extends decision.add_labels), needs_human (~line 1245: same hand-rolled add/remove), and mark_conflito (~line 1355: appends crewflow:conflito). The DISPATCH_DEV branch (~line 1040) fires _dispatch() but NEVER calls set_labels — the todo->dev and dev->review label changes are performed by the one-shot LLM session via gh, which is exactly where the old state fails to be removed.

Primary fix — DISPATCH_DEV (todo->dev): in the dev-dispatch loop in run()/the stage runner, after a successful _dispatch() (i.e. when a session is actually fired and auto_dispatch is on), apply the transition to crewflow:dev atomically via the provider so the issue leaves crewflow:todo immediately and deterministically instead of relying on the LLM. Build the new label set with transition_state(result.item.labels, State.DEV) then add crewflow:running (a modifier, preserved by transition_state) as the executor decision's add_labels indicate, and call provider.set_labels(repo, key, new_labels). Guard with contextlib.suppress/try-except and log, consistent with the existing branches, and respect dry_run (never call set_labels in dry-run). Make sure this does not double-dispatch or race the existing concurrency guards — only transition when the code path already committed to dispatching.

Harden the existing state-changing branches to route state labels through transition_state so exclusivity is guaranteed centrally rather than by ad-hoc list edits: wherever a decision's add_labels contains a crewflow state label (spec/ready/todo/dev/review/qa/done), compute the resulting labels with transition_state(base_labels, <that State>) and then apply the remaining modifier add/remove on top; wherever add_labels contains only modifiers (e.g. crewflow:conflito, crewflow:running, crewflow:changes-requested), keep the current add/remove behavior. A small local helper in deployment.py (e.g. _apply_decision_labels(base_labels, add_labels, remove_labels) -> list[str]) that (1) detects any state label in add_labels and applies transition_state for it, (2) then removes remove_labels, (3) then adds modifier/type labels, is a clean way to centralize this. Import transition_state and State from flow.domain.state.

Do NOT change the executor's decision contract (add_labels/remove_labels stay as-is). The transition enforcement belongs at the set_labels application boundary in deployment.py (and in the domain helper), so the executor stays pure and its existing tests keep passing.

Update flow/prompts/dev.md so the one-shot prompt instructs the agent, when opening the PR, to move to crewflow:review by REMOVING the previous state label in the same operation (e.g. gh issue edit --add-label crewflow:review --remove-label crewflow:dev --remove-label crewflow:todo) — reinforcing the 'exactly 1 state' invariant even on the LLM path. Keep the existing 'remova crewflow:running (mantenha crewflow:review)' instruction. Only edit the MD wording; the engine-side transition is the authoritative guard.

Add integration tests proving no state accumulation. In flow/tests/test_e2e_integration.py (which already builds a mock provider with set_labels mocked) and/or flow/tests/test_deployment_integration.py, add a test that drives an issue through todo -> dev -> review and asserts that after each transition the label set passed to provider.set_labels contains exactly one label from {s.value for s in State}. At minimum assert: after the todo->dev transition, crewflow:todo is absent and crewflow:dev present; and that transition_state guarantees a review transition drops crewflow:dev. Reproduce the #107 scenario: feed labels that already contain two states ({'crewflow:todo','crewflow:review'}) into the label-application path and assert the applied set has exactly one state label.
Run ruff, mypy, and the full suite.
acceptance_criteria: Every set_labels call in deployment.py that changes an issue's state produces a label set with exactly one crewflow state label (verified by routing state changes through transition_state)
The DISPATCH_DEV path applies the todo->dev transition via provider.set_labels (outside dry-run) so the issue leaves crewflow:todo deterministically, not only via the LLM session
Modifiers and type/priority labels are preserved across every transition applied in deployment.py
flow/prompts/dev.md instructs the agent to remove the prior state label when moving to crewflow:review
A test drives todo->dev->review and asserts no state label accumulation (exactly one state label after each transition), including an explicit reproduction of the #107 two-state input
python3.12 -m pytest flow/tests/ -q passes (except the known root-permission failure), ruff clean, mypy clean
findings: Implemented and committed as ae43bda. Added two helpers in deployment/deployment.py: (1) _apply_decision_labels(base, add, remove) which, when add_labels contains a crewflow state label, applies flow.domain.state.transition_state to drop all other states and keep exactly one (preserving modifiers/type/priority/foreign labels), then removes remove_labels and adds non-state add_labels; modifier-only add_labels keep plain add/remove behavior. (2) _apply_dev_transition(provider, repo, issue) which fires only after a dev session is actually dispatched (auto_dispatch on, outside dry-run, _dispatch succeeded and appended to disparadas) and calls provider.set_labels(repo, key, sorted(transition_state(labels, State.DEV) + running)). Wired both dev-dispatch loops (run() ~line 1180 and the _run_stage dev path). Routed rebrand, needs_human, mark_conflito, and the auto-merge review->done branch through _apply_decision_labels for centralized exclusivity. To reach the current labels/key inside the dev loop without changing the (repo, issue, decision) tuple shape (which the dry-run report and multiple unpack sites depend on), _scan_result_to_issue now also carries '_labels' and '_key' in the issue dict (extra keys are harmless to the prompt renderer). Updated flow/prompts/dev.md steps 3 and 7 (and the embedded _DEV_PROMPT_FALLBACK to keep them canonical) so the one-shot agent removes prior state labels in the same gh issue edit; no new template placeholders added. Executor contract unchanged. Added TestStateTransitionExclusivityE2E to flow/tests/test_e2e_integration.py with 5 tests: two-state #107 reproduction via _apply_decision_labels, modifier-only preserves state, _apply_dev_transition removes prior state, full run() todo->dev via provider.set_labels asserts exactly one state + preserved type/priority, and a dev->review domain transition drop-check. Needed collections.abc.Iterable import in deployment.py and the test for clean mypy. Verification: ruff clean (flow/ and deployment/), mypy clean (49 source files, no issues), pytest 586 passed / 1 failed. The single failure is the pre-existing known environmental one: flow/tests/test_prompts_loader.py::TestRenderPromptFallback::test_template_corrompido_ilegivel_usa_fallback (chmod 0o000 ignored because tests run as root) — unrelated and untouched. Baseline was 581 before this feature; +5 new tests = 586. POST-REVIEW HARDENING (semantic review 2026-09-19-163710 NEEDS_CHANGES, Issue 1/3): the dev->review side (the exact transition that produced the #107 accumulation) is now also enforced engine-side, not only by the LLM prompt. Added _apply_review_transition(provider, repo, issue) mirroring _apply_dev_transition: it collapses issue['_labels'] to exactly crewflow:review via transition_state (idempotent no-op when already correct, returns bool) and is called in both reviewer-dispatch loops (run() and _run_stage reviewer stage) right before _dispatch_reviewer, so any stale crewflow:todo/crewflow:dev is stripped in the same set_labels. Because a 2-state issue is AMBIGUOUS and the scanner drops it (parse_state raises EstadoAmbiguo -> current_state=None -> never in scan_results), added a defensive pre-pass _enforce_review_exclusivity(provider, repos, projects) that lists issues by crewflow:review via provider.list_by_state and collapses any carrying an extra state label; it runs before the 'nothing to do' early-return and only outside dry-run. Added domain-pure helper state_labels_present(labels)->set[str] in flow/domain/state.py (never raises, unlike parse_state) to detect the accumulation without I/O. Added 4 engine-path tests to TestStateTransitionExclusivityE2E: _apply_review_transition collapse, its idempotence no-op, run() reviewer path collapsing a parsed-REVIEW issue with residual crewflow:todo, and run() reconciling the ambiguous #107 (todo+review) case that the scanner discards via the _enforce_review_exclusivity pre-pass. Prompt-side dev.md review-transition instruction kept (belt-and-suspenders: the engine defensively enforces but does not observe 'PR just opened' on the dev path, so the session-driven move still matters). Verification: ruff clean (flow/ + deployment/), mypy clean (49 files), pytest 590 passed / 1 failed (same known environmental root+chmod test). 586 + 4 new = 590.
